features.title: Why Marblo?
features.subtitle: Beyond code autocomplete — manage AI agents like a project manager

multiagent.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
multiagent.description: Claude handles backend, GPT/Codex handles frontend, Antigravity runs tests — all simultaneously. Track each agent's progress in real-time on the kanban board.
multiagent.detail:
Marblo's multi-agent system maximizes each AI model's strengths.

Claude handles sophisticated backend logic and architecture design, GPT/Codex delivers rapid frontend coding and UI implementation, and Antigravity manages test writing and code review.

Each agent runs in its own isolated terminal, and you can monitor progress in real-time on the kanban board. Through the MCP protocol, agents share context with each other, collaborating like a real development team.

kanban.title: Kanban Board + Agent Integration
kanban.description: Create tasks and agents automatically pick them up, coding in their own terminals. Todo → In Progress → Done — track every stage on the board.
kanban.detail:
Marblo's kanban board manages agent work through a 5-stage state machine: TODO → CLAIMED → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW → DONE.

When you create a task, it's automatically assigned to the right agent based on role (backend/frontend/test/DevOps). Each agent codes independently in its own terminal, with progress reflected on the kanban board in real-time.

Set up task dependencies (depends_on) to automatically queue tasks until prerequisites are completed.

flow.title: Mission pipelines (coming soon)
flow.description: We're building Mission pipelines that chain multiple steps — code generation → review → testing → deployment — into one automated flow. Until it ships, manage agent work with the Kanban board and task tickets.
flow.detail:
We're building a Mission feature that chains multi-step work into a single automated pipeline.

Until it ships, you can manage agent work by creating tasks on the Kanban board and attaching an agent to a task ticket to review its changes as an inline diff.

orchestrator.title: Natural language Mission Launch (coming soon)
orchestrator.description: We're building a feature that takes a goal in natural language and auto-decomposes it into tasks across agents. Until it ships, create tasks yourself and assign them to role-based agents.
orchestrator.detail:
We're building a feature that takes a natural-language goal like "Add login to this app" and auto-decomposes it into separate tasks.

Until it ships, you can build the same flow by creating tasks on the Kanban board and assigning them to role-based agents (backend / frontend / test).

mcp.title: Native MCP Protocol
mcp.description: Equip agents with file system access, databases, APIs, and more via Model Context Protocol. Agents work in your real development environment.
mcp.detail:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard protocol that provides agents with real development tools and context.

Marblo natively supports MCP, allowing agents to read/write files, query databases, call REST APIs, run Git commands, and more — all in your actual development environment.

Extend agent capabilities by adding custom MCP servers. For example, connect the Marblo MCP server to let agents automatically update task progress on the board.

privacy.title: Local Execution — Your Data Stays on Your Machine
privacy.description: Your code never leaves your machine. The Electron app runs locally — you connect your own existing AI accounts (Claude Code, Codex, etc.). Meets enterprise security requirements.
privacy.detail:
Marblo is an Electron-based desktop app where all code and data is processed exclusively on your local machine.

Your code is never sent to Marblo servers. AI calls go directly to each model provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) using the existing AI accounts you connect (Claude Code / Codex CLI sign-in, or an API key).

Safe for enterprise environments, with on-premise deployment options for enhanced security. Audit logs and SSO authentication are available on the Enterprise plan.

items.q: What is included in the Free plan?
items.a: The Free plan includes 1 project, 5 agents, the kanban board, the terminal and code editor, and MCP integration — free forever. It is enough to get a first feel for Marblo.

items.q: How much is Pro and what is different?
items.a: The Pro plan is ₩19,000/month (about $15). It includes unlimited projects, unlimited agents (fair use · connect your own AI accounts), and the orchestrator, plus everything in Free. Priority support is available from Team Plus and up.

items.q: Are there separate AI usage fees?
items.a: Yes. Each agent runs on your own existing AI account (Claude Code / Codex, etc.) or API key (Claude→Anthropic, GPT/Codex→OpenAI, etc.). After installing, you sign in to those CLIs and connect your accounts. The Marblo fee is the orchestration cost of directing those agents and does not include AI usage fees.

items.q: Is there an annual discount?
items.a: Yes. Choose annual billing and two months are free.

items.q: Are there team or enterprise plans?
items.a: Yes. Team, Team Plus, and Enterprise plans are available, with SSO, audit logs, priority support, and on-premise deployment options.

foundation50Faq.title: Founder FAQ
foundation50Faq.subtitle: Answers to the 5 most common questions before you apply. Further questions go in the #questions Discord channel after you join.
foundation50Faq.q1_body:
Marblo is a heterogeneous AI agent orchestration desktop app. It lets you run Claude, GPT, Antigravity, and local models side by side and direct a fleet of agents through a Kanban board, task tickets, and an integrated terminal.

A 1-minute demo video will land here right before GA. Until then, take a look at the 'Features' and 'Orchestration' sections on the home page for screenshots.
foundation50Faq.q2_title: 2. How do I set up BYOK?
foundation50Faq.q2_body:
On first launch, Marblo opens a settings panel where you register the model keys / subscriptions you want to use. Keys are stored encrypted in your OS keychain and never sent to Marblo servers.

· Claude — issue an API key in the Anthropic console, or sign in with Claude Code Max
· GPT — issue an API key in the OpenAI platform, or sign in with ChatGPT Plus
· Antigravity — sign in with your Google account
· Local models — point Marblo at your Ollama (or compatible) endpoint URL

Register only the models you actually plan to use. You do not have to register all of them.
foundation50Faq.q3_title: 3. How do I submit the thoughtful survey?
foundation50Faq.q3_body:
After using the 1-month beta, submit the 7-question thoughtful survey. The survey link is included in your access and reminder emails.

· ① Usage context ② 'I'll keep using this' / aha moments ③ Where you got stuck / bugs ④ Time & effort vs. the alternative ⑤ Willingness to pay ⑥ Feature to keep / add ⑦ Recommendation score + why
· Real usage evidence and insight matter more than length. You don't have to be flattering — the good, the rough, and improvement requests are all welcome.
· The operator scores it on a 21-point rubric; passing the sincerity bar grants 3 months of Pro. Roughly the top 10 receive a video-interview request, and completing it extends to 6 months.
foundation50Faq.q4_title: 4. How do I get into the Founder Discord?
foundation50Faq.q4_body:
Once your application is reviewed and you're selected, we email access instructions along with a Discord invite link to the email you applied with.

The channel is a private space for Founders only, and your access stays for life even if you cancel Pro later. Inside the channel you get early beta access to new features, a direct line to the developer, and shared workflows among members.
foundation50Faq.q5_body:
Joining the Founder beta is free — there's no payment, so there's nothing to refund.

Marblo Pro free coupon — this is a benefit issued for free when you submit feedback, and it is not refundable. Once you activate Pro with the coupon, no separate refund applies from the start date of use.

Courses (optional purchase) — independent of Founder benefits, you can buy them at full price if you'd like, and under Korean e-commerce law you may withdraw within 7 days of payment.

Founder Discord channel — kept open for life, independent of payment or coupon.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: The questions we hear most often about Marblo.

items.q: What is Marblo?
items.a: Marblo is a desktop app that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents simultaneously on a single kanban board. A central orchestrator splits large work into tickets, assigns them to heterogeneous agents, tracks progress on the board, and puts a human REVIEW gate before anything merges. Beyond just launching several agents, it aims to be a control plane for AI-native teams — tracking tickets, progress, code changes, and reviews in one place — and it runs locally on macOS and Windows.

items.q: How is this different from just using a single CLI or IDE plugin like Claude or Codex?
items.a: A single CLI or IDE plugin is a tool for talking to one agent at a time. Marblo works at the team level on top of that: ① it orchestrates heterogeneous agents — Claude, GPT/Codex, Antigravity — at once, ② it traces work end to end from ticket → agent → PR → diff, ③ it runs agents in isolated git worktrees for safe parallelism, and ④ it keeps a human REVIEW gate before merge. Running agents concurrently is commodity; Marblo's edge is the tracking, decision, and safe-merge layer on top.

items.q: What does the orchestrator actually do?
items.a: The orchestrator is the central agent that directs the team. It breaks large work into file- or module-scoped tickets, assigns each to the best-suited agent, tracks status on the kanban board, and decides the next step when an agent is blocked or finished. You set the direction and just check results at REVIEW.

items.q: Which AI agents does it support?
items.a: It runs heterogeneous agents — Claude, GPT/Codex, and Antigravity — at the same time. It isn't locked to one vendor, and it assigns roles such as backend, frontend, and testing to fit each model's strengths.

items.q: How are model roles assigned?
items.a: Agents are placed by the nature of the work — a top model for complex design, a lighter and cheaper model for repetitive, simple tasks. Everything runs on your own key or subscription (bring your own model), so you decide which model goes where.

items.q: How do I create tickets and the kanban board?
items.a: Define work as a ticket and it lands in the board's TODO column. A ticket can carry a description, an assigned role, and dependencies, and if you describe a goal to the orchestrator it can break large work into several tickets automatically. Agents then claim the tickets and start working.

items.q: How do I track progress?
items.a: Each task moves along the kanban board (TODO → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW → DONE), and you can watch each agent's state and activity log in real time. You can see at a glance which ticket sits with which agent and what it's doing right now.

items.q: Won't multiple agents collide editing the same file?
items.a: When needed, Marblo runs agents in isolated git worktrees so parallel work doesn't step on each other's files. Tasks are split by file or module so ownership doesn't overlap, and each agent's work is merged safely after review.

items.q: How do I review the PRs and code changes (diffs) agents produce?
items.a: When an agent finishes, it opens its result as a PR and the ticket moves to the REVIEW stage. You inspect the changed code (the diff) and approve it or request changes. Only changes that pass the human REVIEW gate get merged, so even amid automation the final decision stays with you.

items.q: How do I move between agents to keep an eye on them?
items.a: On the board you move between agents and terminals quickly with the arrow keys and look right into what each agent is doing. It's designed so you can run many agents at once yet switch easily and never lose the thread.

items.q: What is MCP and why does it matter?
items.a: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI to tools like files, databases, and APIs. Marblo supports MCP natively, so multiple agents share the same tools and context consistently — and collaboration state like tickets and the kanban board flows through MCP too.

items.q: Is my code safe?
items.a: Every agent runs locally on your machine, so your code is not sent to Marblo's servers. Repository, terminal, and file access all happen inside that local boundary, which matters when handling sensitive code and data.

items.q: Do you collect telemetry or usage data?
items.a: Your code and file contents are never sent to or collected by Marblo's servers. We handle only anonymous, non-identifying metrics to improve the product, and any detailed telemetry or third-party sharing is opt-in — active only when you turn it on.

items.q: How much does it cost?
items.a: The Free plan is ₩0/month with core features; the Pro plan is ₩19,000/month (about $15) with unlimited projects and agents (fair use). Priority support starts at Team Plus; Team and Enterprise plans are also available.

items.q: Are there separate AI usage fees?
items.a: Yes. Each agent runs on your own API key or subscription. The Marblo fee is the orchestration cost of directing those agents and does not include AI usage fees (bring your own model).

items.q: Does it work on both Mac and Windows? Does it update automatically?
items.a: Yes. Marblo ships as a desktop app for macOS and Windows. When a new version is released the app checks for and applies the update automatically, so you stay on the latest build.

items.q: How do I get started?
items.a: Download and install the app from the download page, then connect the repository (folder) you want to work in. Create your first ticket, assign an agent, and you're orchestrating right away — and you can try it immediately on the Free plan.

items.q: Where do I download it?
items.a: Get the macOS/Windows app from the download page. You can start right away on the Free plan.

meta.title: Marblo Getting Started Guide — From Install to Your First Mission
meta.description: A step-by-step guide to installing the Marblo desktop app and running your first mission with AI agents. On first launch the required CLIs install automatically — then just authenticate, pick a folder to auto-register your project and auto-start the orchestrator, run your first mission, and set up billing.
meta.heading: Get started with Marblo
meta.subheading: A step-by-step guide from install to your first mission, in the order a new user should follow. Use the table of contents on the left to jump to any step.

install.title: Download, install & first launch
install.intro: First, download and install the Marblo desktop app. macOS and Windows are supported, and the agent CLIs you need install automatically on first launch.

download.title: Get the app from the download page
download.body: On the download page, grab the latest build for your operating system (macOS or Windows). Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, and Windows 10/11, are supported.
download.alt: The Marblo download page showing macOS and Windows build options

run.title: Install and launch for the first time
run.body: Run the installer you downloaded. On macOS, open the .dmg and drag Marblo into your Applications folder; on Windows, follow the installer prompts.
run.warn: On first launch you may see a macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen warning. On macOS, choose 'Open Anyway' under System Settings > Privacy & Security; on Windows, choose 'More info > Run anyway'. The builds are properly signed.
run.alt: The Marblo welcome screen shown on first launch

autocli.title: Required CLIs & Marblo MCP install automatically
autocli.body: On first launch, Marblo automatically installs the required agent CLIs (Claude Code · Codex · Antigravity) and the Marblo MCP. There's no need to install anything from a Harness tab — just wait a moment for the install to finish.
autocli.note: There's nothing to install yourself. In the next step you only need to log in (authenticate) to each CLI, and you're ready to go.
autocli.alt: Marblo automatically installing the required CLIs and MCP on first launch

auth.title: Authenticate the CLIs (log in)
auth.intro: Because the required CLIs install automatically, your only setup task is to log in (authenticate) to each CLI.

claude.title: Log in to Claude Code
claude.body: Run the command below in a terminal and follow the prompt to sign in with your Anthropic account in the browser.

codex.title: Log in to Codex
codex.body: Log in to Codex the same way, authenticating with your OpenAI account.

antigravity.title: Authenticate Antigravity
antigravity.body: Authenticate Antigravity as well. Follow the sign-in prompt that appears the first time you use it to log in with your account.
antigravity.note: You only need to authenticate the CLIs you'll actually use. To run multiple agents at once, authenticate all of them.

byom.title: Connect a model with BYOM
byom.body: There are two ways to connect models: sign in to a native CLI account, or add a vendor key through Bring Your Own Model (BYOM). With a vendor key, agents boot against that model instead of a native CLI account. Supported choices include GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, and local models through Ollama.
byom.note: Native CLI authentication and BYOM are separate paths. Use the native CLI login for Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity; use BYOM when you want to bring a vendor key or a local Ollama model.

verify.title: Verify authentication
verify.body: Once you're signed in, each CLI switches to an authenticated state. If the status doesn't update, try restarting the app.
verify.tip: Credentials are stored locally by each CLI — Marblo never stores your account password or API keys, and everything runs on your own machine.

project.title: Pick a folder — project auto-registers
project.intro: Just pick the code folder you want to work in — with no confirmation step, the project registers automatically and the orchestrator starts alongside it.

add.title: Pick a folder = zero-click registration
add.body: Select a local folder and Marblo registers it as a project right away. There's no 'Do you want to register?' confirmation click — picking the folder is all it takes. You can switch between registered projects from the sidebar.
add.tip: A git repository is recommended. Marblo runs multiple agents safely in parallel using isolated git worktrees and tracks changes as diffs.
add.alt: Picking a folder in Marblo auto-registers it as a project with zero clicks

orchestrator.title: The orchestrator auto-starts
orchestrator.body: Once the project is registered, the orchestrator starts automatically and opens a dedicated terminal session. It analyzes your request, breaks it into tickets, and spawns agents with an assigned role (frontend, backend, etc.) and model (Claude, GPT/Codex, Antigravity).
orchestrator.note: We recommend running a small task with a single agent first to get comfortable with the flow, then scaling up to multiple agents at once.
orchestrator.alt: The orchestrator auto-starting the moment a project is registered

mission.title: Run your first mission / flow
mission.intro: Now it's time to give real work. Hand your first mission to the orchestrator.

create.title: Write a mission
create.body: Describe the feature you want to build or the bug you want to fix in plain language to the orchestrator. It breaks this down into tickets on the kanban board.
create.alt: A mission broken down into tickets on the kanban board

run.title: Run & track progress
run.body: While agents work through tickets in parallel, you can track progress in real time on the kanban board. Each agent's terminal output is available in its own tab.

review.title: The review gate
review.body: Finished tickets move to the REVIEW state. A human confirms the changes and approves them before they're merged.
review.warn: Always review the diff before merging an agent's changes. Marblo places a human REVIEW gate before merge so unintended changes don't land automatically.

modelRouting.title: The orchestrator routes models across the fleet
modelRouting.body: The orchestrator turns your goal into a ticket graph, then spawns a model suited to each task. It considers task shape, cost, and available quota when selecting models, and diversifies the fleet so the whole mission is not locked to one vendor.
modelRouting.tip: You can follow each ticket's assigned model in the Board and Agents views. The model used for a task can differ from the model running the orchestrator.

lanes.title: Run Quick Lanes in parallel
lanes.intro: Quick Lanes are the direct, hands-on mode: choose a model yourself and start several agents side by side without going through the orchestrator.

start.title: Start a lane directly
start.body: Open the Lanes tab, create a lane, describe the work, and start it. Repeat for as many independent tasks as you want; each lane runs alongside the others.
start.alt: The Quick Lanes tab showing several parallel lane cards

model.title: Choose the model for each lane
model.body: Each lane has its own model selector. Pick the model that fits that task, including a BYOM or local option when it is available in your model registry.
model.note: Quick Lanes do not ask the orchestrator to decompose or route the work. You choose the model and the parallel work yourself.

isolation.title: Track lane progress independently
isolation.body: Lane work is tagged with its own lane context and runs in an isolated worktree. Open a lane's terminal or details to follow status, model, worktree state, and restart actions without mixing it with mission tickets.
isolation.alt: A Quick Lane detail view with its model, terminal, and isolated worktree status

workspace.title: Explore the workspace tabs
workspace.intro: After your first mission, use the workspace tabs to move from planning to live execution, review, and the audit trail. Each tab has one focused job.

board.title: Board — see the kanban flow
board.body: Board is the kanban view of project tickets. Use it to see what is queued, in progress, in review, or done, and open a ticket to inspect its agent and changes.
board.alt: The Board tab showing project tickets across kanban columns

agents.title: Agents — watch live terminals
agents.body: Agents gives you a live terminal for each agent and its current status. The agent watchdog can reconnect or self-heal interrupted work, while the panel keeps the latest model and activity visible.
agents.alt: The Agents tab showing live agent terminals and status cards

code.title: Code — review worktree diffs
code.body: Code opens the files and diff for the selected worktree. Use it to inspect the exact changes and leave review feedback before anything is merged.
code.alt: The Code tab showing a worktree diff before merge

worktrees.title: Worktrees — keep tickets isolated
worktrees.body: Worktrees shows the isolated branch and filesystem workspace created for each ticket. Parallel agents work in separate worktrees, so unrelated changes do not collide while they are being developed.
worktrees.alt: The Worktrees tab showing isolated ticket workspaces

lanes.title: Lanes — run direct parallel work
lanes.body: Lanes is the direct parallel mode described above: select a model per lane and run independent agents next to orchestrated mission work.
lanes.alt: The Lanes tab showing user-selected models for parallel work

usage.title: Usage — understand model and daily cost
usage.body: Usage summarizes agent and model activity over time, including daily cost totals where recorded. Use it to understand which vendors and models are consuming your available budget or quota.
usage.alt: The Usage tab showing agent, model, and daily cost summaries

history.title: History — keep the append-only record
history.body: History is the append-only work ledger: progress, costs, provenance, and merge events stay available after a task completes. Use it to reconstruct what happened and open the related ticket or diff.
history.alt: The History tab showing an append-only work and merge ledger

billing.title: Billing & plans
billing.intro: Marblo is free to start, and you can upgrade to Pro when you need more.

plans.title: Explore the plans
plans.body: The Free plan gives you the core features at no cost. Pro is a monthly subscription with additional features. See the pricing page for the differences.
plans.note: Usage fees for the agent CLIs (Claude, Codex, Antigravity) are billed separately to each provider account and are independent of your Marblo subscription.

manage.title: Manage your subscription
manage.body: After signing in, view and manage your subscription status and billing history from your account.

faq.title: FAQ & help
faq.intro: If you get stuck, the resources below can help.

links.title: Learn more
links.body: Find answers to common questions in the FAQ, and report a bug if something goes wrong. Take a look at the Founder program too.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.subtitle: Review and manage your current plan and billing status.

change_plan.title: Change plan
change_plan.desc: Upgrade or switch to a different plan on the pricing page.

history.title: Billing history
history.coming_soon: Detailed billing history (receipts) is coming soon. For now, only the current billing period is shown.

cancel.title: Cancel subscription
cancel.desc: Canceling stops auto-renewal immediately. If paid time remains, you keep access until the period ends (no refund).
cancel.desc_past_due: Payment failed and retries are scheduled. Canceling stops further charges. If paid time remains, you keep access until the period ends (no refund).
cancel.confirm: Are you sure you want to cancel? Auto-renewal stops, and you move to Free after the remaining period (no refund).
cancel.confirm_past_due: Payment has failed. Canceling stops retry charges. If paid time remains, you keep access until the period ends (no refund). Continue?
cancel.error: Something went wrong while canceling. Please try again shortly.

subscription.app_hint: You can also view your subscription status from the account menu in the desktop app.

replay.privacyNote: This page is a public copy that the Marblo app redacted on the author's machine. Secrets, local paths, and personal data are removed at every visibility level. If the author unpublishes it, copies may still remain in external caches and social previews.
